items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: we had a saxophone player, Ray Perry, who played third alto, who played violin like Fiddler Williams you know?

ctx.x: And Hamp was quite a showman, wasn’t he, at that time?

Oh yeah. Hamp’s band was some band. It was an exciting band to play in, it was a very innovative band, and it was a new style, it was a completely different sound they had. A very exciting band, a bunch of young fellas in there, Ernie Royal, Joe Newman and guys like that, Illinois Jacquet, Dexter Gordon, they were all in that band. Irving Ashby, who later was with Nat King Cole, the guitarist. And speaking of, we had a saxophone player, Ray Perry, who played third alto, who played violin like Fiddler Williams you…
Did you have an opportunity to go overseas a lot?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Had Ray Perry playing third alto, and he played violin like most of the guys improvised playing on a wind instrument.

ctx.x: Was it more harmonically, or rhythmically, or a combination of both?

Both. A combination of both. Much more daring than the other bands had been. The other bands, by comparison, were very subdued. This was a very exciting band, and the guys were exciting too. They all had different styles. Illinois Jacquet and Dexter Gordon, they were exciting, but then you had Jack McVey playing baritone saxophone, who was as exciting on the baritone as Illinois and Dexter were on the tenors. Had Ray Perry playing third alto, and he played violin like most of the guys improvised playing on a wind…
Did you find you changed your own style to fit into the band?
